Databricks, Spark & Delta Lake / Spark &.question: Explain Spark execution at a high level.
Databricks, Spark & Delta Lake / Spark &.reference_answer: In Spark, the driver prepares the execution plan and schedules tasks, while executors run those tasks on data partitions. Each partition is a unit of parallel work. If partitions are skewed, some tasks take much longer than others; if there are too many small partitions, scheduling overhead increases. When tuning Databricks pipelines, I examine the Spark UI for stage time, shuffle, skew and task distribution before changing cluster size or partition settings.
Databricks, Spark & Delta Lake / Spark &.technical_context: Driver constructs query plans and schedules stages. Executors hold cores/memory and execute task partitions; shuffle can move data across machines. Too few partitions waste parallelism, too many tiny partitions add overhead.
common_mistakes: Treating the driver as processing all large rows
Increasing partitions blindly
Ignoring skew and shuffle
Databricks, Spark & Delta Lake / Spark &.project_context: Your Databricks ingestion and anomaly analytics rely on Spark job planning and appropriate cluster sizing.

Databricks, Spark & Delta Lake / Spark &.question: Why does a PySpark transformation not run immediately?
Databricks, Spark & Delta Lake / Spark &.reference_answer: Spark is lazily evaluated. Transformations such as select, join and filter describe what should happen, but they do not immediately process the full dataset. An action like count or a write triggers a job. The driver builds a DAG, optimizes the plan and splits stages around shuffles. When investigating a slow Databricks workflow, I inspect the physical plan and stage metrics, especially repeated scans and unnecessary wide transformations.
Databricks, Spark & Delta Lake / Spark &.technical_context: Operations like select/filter form a logical DAG and Catalyst/physical planning optimize execution. A count or write starts a job, and stages split at shuffle dependencies. Reusing uncached transformations may recompute upstream work.
common_mistakes: Assuming transformations always execute immediately
Calling count repeatedly without reason
Ignoring shuffle boundaries
Databricks, Spark & Delta Lake / Spark &.project_context: Your Azure Databricks file-processing jobs can use lazy plans to push filters early and avoid repeated scans.

Databricks, Spark & Delta Lake / Spark &.question: How do you optimize a slow join?
Databricks, Spark & Delta Lake / Spark &.reference_answer: When joining in Spark, the expensive part is often moving rows across executors by join keys. If one side is truly small, a broadcast join can copy it to workers and avoid shuffling the large dataset. For two large tables, I inspect the plan, partitioning and skewed keys. In our pipeline RCA model, broadcasting small metadata can help, but I measure actual job time and executor memory rather than forcing broadcast everywhere.
Databricks, Spark & Delta Lake / Spark &.technical_context: For joins, inspect size/cardinality and key skew. Sort-merge or shuffle-hash joins repartition by key; broadcast hash join distributes a suitably small table, limited by memory and configuration.
common_mistakes: Broadcasting an oversized table
Ignoring many-to-many row explosion
Assuming broadcast always faster
Databricks, Spark & Delta Lake / Spark &.project_context: Your anomaly RCA queries join activity logs, dependencies and run history in Databricks.

Databricks, Spark & Delta Lake / Spark &.question: What is adaptive query execution?
Databricks, Spark & Delta Lake / Spark &.reference_answer: I tune partitions, caching and adaptive execution based on Spark UI evidence. Partition count controls parallel tasks, but uneven keys create slow stragglers. AQE can adjust shuffle partitions or join strategies during execution. Caching helps only when data is reused and memory pressure is acceptable. For production Databricks pipelines, I benchmark representative workloads and verify costs, spills, skew and elapsed time rather than applying every tuning switch by default.
Databricks, Spark & Delta Lake / Spark &.technical_context: Adaptive Query Execution can coalesce shuffle partitions and handle skewed joins. Cache only repeatedly reused datasets that fit resources, unpersist after use and avoid high-cardinality partition columns for tables.
common_mistakes: Caching every DataFrame
Over-partitioning on unique IDs
Assuming AQE fixes all poor join keys
Databricks, Spark & Delta Lake / Spark &.project_context: Your Databricks operations included Spark tuning and capacity management; each optimization should have measured before/after metrics.

Databricks, Spark & Delta Lake / Spark &.question: When would you use Spark SQL instead of PySpark?
Databricks, Spark & Delta Lake / Spark &.reference_answer: I choose Spark SQL for readable joins, aggregations and reporting logic that analysts can review, and PySpark DataFrames for programmatic data pipelines, complex schemas and reusable Python functions. Both generally use Spark's Catalyst optimizer, so choosing SQL instead of DataFrames does not automatically make a job faster. I compare explain plans, joins, shuffle stages and data volumes. I also avoid collecting distributed data into local Python unnecessarily, because that can make a scalable job slow or unstable.
Databricks, Spark & Delta Lake / Spark &.technical_context: Both Spark SQL and PySpark DataFrame operations are translated into Spark logical plans, optimized by Catalyst and executed in distributed stages. SQL suits existing SQL teams, concise analytics and view-oriented logic; DataFrames suit reusable Python functions, schema-driven transformations, conditional workflows and composition with other Spark APIs. Avoid confusing PySpark DataFrames with ordinary local Python loops or pandas: collecting large partitions into the driver negates distributed execution. Compare physical plans and shuffle volume rather than assuming one interface is always faster.
common_mistakes: Assuming PySpark means per-row Python execution for every DataFrame expression
Calling collect() on a large dataset
Comparing performance without the physical plans
Databricks, Spark & Delta Lake / Spark &.project_context: For governed reporting tables, use SQL for shared transformations and PySpark when complex validation rules are packaged as reusable transformations.

Databricks, Spark & Delta Lake / Delta L.question: Why is Delta different from a normal relational table?
Databricks, Spark & Delta Lake / Delta L.reference_answer: Delta Lake uses a transaction log on top of Parquet files to provide ACID-style table operations. Each commit records a new table version, and readers use a consistent snapshot rather than seeing partially written files. MERGE supports row-level changes and time travel can examine earlier committed versions within retention. In our Databricks pipelines, this is more robust than treating a folder of arbitrary Parquet files as a transactional relational table.
Databricks, Spark & Delta Lake / Delta L.technical_context: Delta stores immutable Parquet data plus _delta_log actions recording adds/removes and schema/protocol metadata. Readers use a consistent snapshot; concurrent writers coordinate optimistic transactions. Retention/vacuum rules affect time travel.
common_mistakes: Assuming all Parquet folders are ACID
Vacuuming before needed history retention
Ignoring concurrent writer conflicts
Databricks, Spark & Delta Lake / Delta L.project_context: Your ADF/Databricks systems depend on reliable incremental updates and read-consistent Delta tables.

Databricks, Spark & Delta Lake / Delta L.question: How do you recover a deleted Delta table version?
Databricks, Spark & Delta Lake / Delta L.reference_answer: In Delta Lake, time travel reads an earlier snapshot using its transaction log, while RESTORE creates a new current version based on an older snapshot. For debugging, I first check table history and compare the affected rows. If a restore is approved, I verify that the files are still retained, then run the RESTORE and validate downstream jobs. I also check retention and CDC impacts because removing historical files with VACUUM can limit how far back we can travel.
Databricks, Spark & Delta Lake / Delta L.technical_context: Delta maintains transaction-log versions and references retained data files. Query `VERSION AS OF` or `TIMESTAMP AS OF` to inspect historical snapshots. RESTORE creates a new transaction-log commit representing a previous state; VACUUM retention can remove files required for history. For an accidental overwrite, identify the correct version and check downstream change-data consumers before restoring.
common_mistakes: Treating RESTORE as deleting all newer history
Forgetting retention/VACUUM
Restoring without checking downstream reads
Databricks, Spark & Delta Lake / Delta L.project_context: Your Databricks pipelines can use table history for incident forensics, but choose a restore plan that accounts for dependent workflows and data retention.

Databricks, Spark & Delta Lake / Delta L.question: How do you handle source/destination column mismatch?
Databricks, Spark & Delta Lake / Delta L.reference_answer: Delta schema enforcement prevents a pipeline from silently writing incompatible columns or types. When legitimate source changes occur, I choose an explicit evolution strategy, such as adding a nullable column with mergeSchema where supported, and test downstream consumers. I do not simply turn on unrestricted auto-merge for every job. In enterprise ingestion, schema contracts and alerts are essential because a technically successful write can still break reporting semantics.
Databricks, Spark & Delta Lake / Delta L.technical_context: Delta validates write schema by default; explicit mergeSchema/autoMerge options control evolution. Distinguish adding nullable columns from unsafe type changes; track producer/consumer contracts and quality tests.
common_mistakes: Assuming autoMerge fixes incompatible types
Ignoring downstream dashboards
Evolving schema without governance
Databricks, Spark & Delta Lake / Delta L.project_context: Your data pipelines handle differences between incoming files and curated table columns in Databricks.

Databricks, Spark & Delta Lake / Delta L.question: How do you implement incremental processing in Delta?
Databricks, Spark & Delta Lake / Delta L.reference_answer: For incremental Delta ingestion, I extract changed source records using a watermark or CDC feed, deduplicate them by business key and source update time, and MERGE them into the destination. I explicitly handle late data and deletions so stale rows do not remain. MERGE gives transactionally consistent upserts, but a bad key can duplicate data or overwrite the wrong record. I monitor changed-row counts and run reconciliation checks.
Databricks, Spark & Delta Lake / Delta L.technical_context: Define a stable business key and deduplicate source rows before merge; use change sequence/watermark carefully, account for late-arriving data and handle source deletes where appropriate. Partition pruning and file layout affect performance.
common_mistakes: Merging duplicated source keys
Ignoring late data or deletes
Using a non-unique key
Databricks, Spark & Delta Lake / Delta L.project_context: Your ADF and Databricks projects use parameterized incremental loads and upserts.

Databricks, Spark & Delta Lake / Delta L.question: What does OPTIMIZE do?
Databricks, Spark & Delta Lake / Delta L.reference_answer: Delta OPTIMIZE is mainly about file layout. Repeated small writes create many tiny Parquet files, making later queries spend extra time on metadata and opening files. Compaction combines them into better-sized data files without changing logical table rows. I benchmark read performance and compaction costs before scheduling it. I distinguish OPTIMIZE from VACUUM, which removes eligible old files and can affect time travel retention.
Databricks, Spark & Delta Lake / Delta L.technical_context: Small-file overhead increases metadata operations and I/O scheduling. Bin-packing reduces file counts; consider auto-compaction, optimized writes and vacuum/retention separately. Compaction is not equivalent to clustering or deleting history.
common_mistakes: Equating OPTIMIZE with VACUUM
Compacting too frequently
Assuming all slow reads are file-count problems
Databricks, Spark & Delta Lake / Delta L.project_context: Your Databricks cost optimization work can include identifying excessive file counts and inefficient read patterns.

Databricks, Spark & Delta Lake / Delta L.question: How does liquid clustering differ from Z-ORDER?
Databricks, Spark & Delta Lake / Delta L.reference_answer: I use file layout techniques to reduce how much data a query scans. Z-ORDER reorganizes data files around chosen filter columns during optimization. Liquid clustering provides a more flexible clustering model for supported Delta tables and lets keys evolve with workloads. I would not enable both indiscriminately; I check runtime compatibility, query filters, data size and maintenance cost. The real success metric is scan reduction and query time on representative workloads.
Databricks, Spark & Delta Lake / Delta L.technical_context: Z-ORDER colocates values of specified columns during OPTIMIZE; liquid clustering uses a clustering-key configuration and incremental layout maintenance. Supported runtime/table-feature constraints matter; benchmark realistic selective predicates.
common_mistakes: Applying Z-ORDER to every column
Mixing incompatible features
Ignoring query predicate patterns
Databricks, Spark & Delta Lake / Delta L.project_context: Your Databricks interview preparation includes OPTIMIZE, Z-ORDER and liquid clustering trade-offs.

Databricks, Spark & Delta Lake / Databri.question: How did your team optimize cluster spend?
Databricks, Spark & Delta Lake / Databri.reference_answer: I use jobs compute for scheduled production workloads and interactive compute for development or exploration. Job clusters can be provisioned for a run and terminated afterward, reducing idle cost and isolating production execution. The trade-off is startup time and choosing the right capacity. For our Databricks platform I would compare job duration, queueing, autoscaling, utilization and DBU/cloud cost before migrating workflows.
Databricks, Spark & Delta Lake / Databri.technical_context: Compare startup overhead, auto-termination, workload isolation, access modes, spot/on-demand use and cost attribution. Jobs can use ephemeral compute while shared interactive clusters may incur idle charges.
common_mistakes: Keeping large clusters idle
Ignoring job startup overhead
Reusing interactive clusters for every production pipeline
Databricks, Spark & Delta Lake / Databri.project_context: Your Databricks platform work targeted compute right-sizing and operating-cost reduction.

Databricks, Spark & Delta Lake / Databri.question: How can you identify whether compute autoscaling is enabled?
Databricks, Spark & Delta Lake / Databri.reference_answer: A fixed-size cluster has a set worker count, while an autoscaling cluster can vary workers between configured minimum and maximum limits. I choose based on workload variation, startup sensitivity, skew and cost. For a heavy but brief batch, autoscaling or task-specific job compute may help; stable loads may benefit from predictable fixed capacity. I check the actual compute configuration and metrics instead of assuming every job cluster is dynamically sized.
Databricks, Spark & Delta Lake / Databri.technical_context: Autoscale responds to observed resource conditions but adds allocation delay and may not fix data skew. Job compute and autoscaling are separate concepts; UI visibility depends on policy and access mode.
common_mistakes: Assuming job cluster always means autoscaling
Expecting autoscale to fix poor Spark joins
Setting maximum workers without budget controls
Databricks, Spark & Delta Lake / Databri.project_context: Your Databricks operations included capacity planning and selecting job compute for higher-load tasks.

Databricks, Spark & Delta Lake / Databri.question: What changed during Unity Catalog migration?
Databricks, Spark & Delta Lake / Databri.reference_answer: Unity Catalog is Databricks’ centralized governance layer for tables, views, volumes and other assets. It organizes objects under catalogs and schemas and supports fine-grained access grants and lineage. When moving existing workloads from legacy metastore governance, I check table locations, service identities, permissions and job dependencies before cutover. In my platform story the value is consistent access control and visibility into data use, rather than simply renaming schemas. I would validate that unauthorized users cannot read restricted datasets.
Databricks, Spark & Delta Lake / Databri.technical_context: Unity Catalog provides a metastore hierarchy such as catalog.schema.table, central permissions, lineage and supported data governance features. Workspaces attach to metastores and workloads use authorized identities; migration from legacy Hive metastore requires checking grants, external locations, paths and jobs. Governance depends on configured privileges, not the mere existence of a catalog.
common_mistakes: Granting broad catalog privileges
Breaking old job paths after migration
Assuming schema hierarchy alone ensures isolation
Databricks, Spark & Delta Lake / Databri.project_context: Your Databricks migration story includes Unity Catalog and should be tied to concrete grants, testing, lineage and workload cutover evidence.

Databricks, Spark & Delta Lake / Databri.question: What is a materialized view in a Spark declarative pipeline?
Databricks, Spark & Delta Lake / Databri.reference_answer: In a declarative data pipeline I define the datasets and transformations I want, instead of manually sequencing every notebook task. The system derives dependencies and manages refresh, with capabilities varying by pipeline type and runtime. I still add data quality expectations, lineage and monitoring. For a materialized summary table I verify refresh behavior and freshness requirements rather than assuming every aggregation updates incrementally. This keeps production orchestration observable and governed.
Databricks, Spark & Delta Lake / Databri.technical_context: Managed pipelines handle table definitions, streaming/batch refresh, quality expectations and dependency scheduling depending on available runtime features. Verify whether materialized views refresh incrementally and use governance controls.
common_mistakes: Assuming all views are automatically fresh
Ignoring quality expectations
Confusing declarative pipelines with ordinary SQL views
Databricks, Spark & Delta Lake / Databri.project_context: Your Databricks studies include materialized views and declarative pipeline operations in addition to ADF orchestration.

Databricks, Spark & Delta Lake / Databri.question: How do you investigate a failed Databricks job?
Databricks, Spark & Delta Lake / Databri.reference_answer: I use Databricks Workflows to define the sequence of ingestion, transformation and validation tasks, with clear dependencies and retry rules. Monitoring includes failed stages, run duration, cluster usage and data quality, not only whether the final status is green. Our anomaly RCA approach adds statistical baselines and linked activity logs to detect unusual runs before SLA impact. Correlated task IDs help support engineers identify the actual bottleneck.
Databricks, Spark & Delta Lake / Databri.technical_context: Model tasks as DAG with conditional paths and alerts, set timeouts, parameterize jobs and record run/attempt IDs. Observe retries, task durations, data quality and cost together; preserve idempotency.
common_mistakes: Retrying writes without deduplication
Watching job success only
Losing activity-level correlations
Databricks, Spark & Delta Lake / Databri.project_context: Your anomaly RCA assistant monitors pipeline duration anomalies and correlates activity logs and dependencies.

Databricks, Spark & Delta Lake / Databri.question: How would you explain the 27% cost improvement?
Databricks, Spark & Delta Lake / Databri.reference_answer: For compute cost reduction I first establish the monthly cost, DBU and VM usage, workload volume, job failure rate and SLAs. Then I right-size long-running workloads, replace idle shared compute with job clusters where suitable and tune Spark joins or partitions that waste CPU and shuffle time. I compare like-for-like periods, not just cluster sizes, and make sure reliability and latency have not worsened. A percentage saving is credible only when it is reconciled with billing and a documented baseline.
Databricks, Spark & Delta Lake / Databri.technical_context: A defensible Databricks saving is workload normalized. Separate DBUs, VM compute, storage and job frequency, then measure total spend before and after while holding comparable data volume, SLAs and success rate. Use ephemeral job compute for scheduled batch jobs, automatic termination, right-sized workers, Photon where appropriate, partition pruning, shuffle tuning and workload concurrency limits. Test that smaller compute does not increase retries, latency or downstream cost. Attribute savings to documented baselines; avoid suggesting a team achieved a percentage that accounting has not verified.
common_mistakes: Counting smaller nodes as savings without measuring runtime
Ignoring extra retry cost
Using one team's savings percentage as a guaranteed result elsewhere
Databricks, Spark & Delta Lake / Databri.project_context: Explain the previously reported 27% Databricks operational cost reduction as a team achievement supported by capacity planning, job compute and Spark configuration changes; validate against billing data.

Databricks, Spark & Delta Lake / Databri.question: What belongs in a Databricks DR plan?
Databricks, Spark & Delta Lake / Databri.reference_answer: I begin disaster recovery by classifying critical workloads and defining RPO, the acceptable data loss, and RTO, the acceptable recovery duration. Then I design backups or replication, infrastructure recovery, secrets and metadata restoration and a clear failover runbook. I rehearse restoring a representative pipeline, not merely checking that backup files exist. For Databricks workloads I also account for jobs, Unity Catalog permissions, storage paths and external integrations.
Databricks, Spark & Delta Lake / Databri.technical_context: Define RPO and RTO, protect storage and metadata backups, infrastructure as code, restore identities/secrets and validate alternate-region dependencies. A backup without a tested restore does not demonstrate recovery.
common_mistakes: Treating replication as complete DR
Ignoring identity/config recovery
Never testing restore
Databricks, Spark & Delta Lake / Databri.project_context: Your platform leadership work included disaster recovery planning for cloud data services.

ADF, Data Pipelines & Modelling / Azure.question: What is the role of a linked service?
ADF, Data Pipelines & Modelling / Azure.reference_answer: A linked service is the connection definition for a source or destination, such as Azure SQL, ADLS or Key Vault. A dataset describes the specific table, file path and format used by an activity. The integration runtime provides the execution and network boundary for movement. When moving an ADF pipeline from Dev to QA, I review environment parameters, linked service endpoints, identity and dataset paths because a QA deployment can still accidentally point to a Dev database.
ADF, Data Pipelines & Modelling / Azure.technical_context: Azure Data Factory separates linked services, datasets, integration runtimes and activities. A linked service defines connector details and authentication, often using managed identity and a Key Vault reference. A dataset binds a location, file format, table or schema to that connector, optionally with parameters. A Copy activity consumes source and sink datasets. Environments must use distinct validated endpoint and credential configuration, so a QA pipeline does not accidentally read Dev data. Secret values must not be embedded in pipeline JSON or logs.
common_mistakes: Treating a linked service as a table schema
Hardcoding credentials in datasets
Promoting QA while leaving a Dev connector selected
ADF, Data Pipelines & Modelling / Azure.project_context: During Dev-to-QA promotion, confirm the QA linked service actually resolves to QA and check integration runtime networking before executing a copy.

ADF, Data Pipelines & Modelling / Azure.question: What if a QA linked service points to Dev?
ADF, Data Pipelines & Modelling / Azure.reference_answer: ADF Copy activity is for moving data between sources and sinks using defined connectors and column mappings. I check the linked services, integration runtime, schemas, nullability, data types and fault policies before running it. If columns change between source and destination, I decide whether the pipeline should reject the change or apply an approved mapping. After the copy, I compare source and target counts, rejected rows and control totals, instead of assuming a successful activity status means all data is correct.
ADF, Data Pipelines & Modelling / Azure.technical_context: Copy activity supports source/sink connectors, explicit column mapping, type conversion, fault handling and staging options. Diagnose schema drift by comparing source columns and sink contracts and deliberately choosing strict mapping versus allowed additions. Validate the configured integration runtime, throughput and network path; a connection pointing at Dev is a deployment configuration defect rather than a data mapping fix. Audit row counts, rejected records and copy metrics. For complex calculations or upserts, use suitable downstream transformations, SQL procedures or Delta merge instead.
common_mistakes: Assuming Copy activity replaces complex transformations
Treating success status as row-level correctness
Leaving QA linked to a Dev database
ADF, Data Pipelines & Modelling / Azure.project_context: When copying reporting tables from Dev to QA, first verify the QA linked service target, then check explicit mapping and row reconciliation.

ADF, Data Pipelines & Modelling / Azure.question: Explain an ADF incremental load.
ADF, Data Pipelines & Modelling / Azure.reference_answer: In an incremental ADF load, I persist the last committed watermark, capture a new upper bound and query source rows inside that interval. I land the results, deduplicate and merge them into the destination using a stable key. Only after the destination transaction and quality checks succeed do I advance the watermark. I also plan for late records, equal timestamps, timezone consistency and deletes. For those cases CDC or overlap windows are often safer than relying only on updated timestamps.
ADF, Data Pipelines & Modelling / Azure.technical_context: A high-watermark pipeline reads the last successfully processed timestamp or version, chooses an upper bound for the current run and extracts rows in a defined interval such as updated_at greater than the previous watermark and less than or equal to the upper bound. Land and merge with a stable business key so retries do not duplicate records. Update the watermark only after validation and destination commit. Time-based watermarks can miss late arrivals or deletes; use a safety overlap, change tracking or CDC when the source supports it, and reconcile counts.
common_mistakes: Advancing watermark before target commit
Ignoring records sharing the same timestamp
Expecting updated_at alone to detect hard deletes
ADF, Data Pipelines & Modelling / Azure.project_context: ADF controls extraction windows while Databricks Delta MERGE makes reruns idempotent; CDC handles deletes where the source exposes them.

ADF, Data Pipelines & Modelling / Azure.question: How do you handle concurrent SHIR jobs?
ADF, Data Pipelines & Modelling / Azure.reference_answer: A self-hosted integration runtime is an ADF execution and connectivity bridge for private or on-premises systems. Concurrent copy activity performance depends on runtime capacity and source throughput; I monitor queued versus running jobs, CPU, memory and network, then scale or tune concurrency cautiously. For production sizing I measure actual concurrent activities and runtime nodes against network saturation, source throttling and copy queue delay. Adding parallelism can worsen reliability when the underlying database cannot keep up.
ADF, Data Pipelines & Modelling / Azure.technical_context: The runtime is a managed Windows agent that executes copy/lookup/connectivity for supported connectors while communicating outbound to Azure control services. Throughput depends on node capacity, concurrent job limits, source/sink constraints and network. Scale out nodes and monitor queues before increasing parallelism.
common_mistakes: Assuming concurrent ADF triggers equal concurrent runtime execution
Ignoring source database limits
Opening inbound internet access unnecessarily
ADF, Data Pipelines & Modelling / Azure.project_context: For enterprise Azure Data Factory pipelines, diagnose concurrency against both self-hosted runtime queueing and backend database pressure.

ADF, Data Pipelines & Modelling / Azure.question: How do you promote ADF from Dev to QA?
ADF, Data Pipelines & Modelling / Azure.reference_answer: I parameterize the pipeline for file locations, table names and runtime behavior instead of copying the entire ADF pipeline for each environment. Linked services and datasets use their own parameters, while identities and secrets stay environment-specific. During promotion I review the deployment configuration, verify integration runtime connectivity and run a small reconciliation test. I particularly check that a QA linked service cannot silently target the Dev database, because that is an easy way to contaminate downstream testing.
ADF, Data Pipelines & Modelling / Azure.technical_context: ADF pipeline parameters describe runtime inputs, while linked service and dataset parameters bind environment-specific endpoints, object names and paths. A deployable artifact should separate code from configuration, resolve secrets through Key Vault/managed identities and apply validation before deployment. Dev/QA/Prod should have isolated data targets, identities, integration runtimes and approval gates. Keep typed/default parameters understandable; never allow untrusted user input to select arbitrary storage accounts or production tables. Add smoke tests that prove QA is not accidentally wired to Dev.
common_mistakes: Hardcoding Dev hostnames into QA
Allowing arbitrary user-supplied database targets
Copying production secrets into templates
ADF, Data Pipelines & Modelling / Azure.project_context: A Dev-to-QA reporting-table copy uses the same pipeline logic but explicit QA linked services, schema mappings and feature-branch validation.

ADF, Data Pipelines & Modelling / Azure.question: How can you find ADF runs taking over 15 minutes?
ADF, Data Pipelines & Modelling / Azure.reference_answer: For ADF runtime troubleshooting I first check that pipeline and activity diagnostic logs are being sent to the correct Log Analytics workspace. Then I write a KQL query limited to the affected resource and time period, calculate or inspect runtime, and filter activity runs exceeding fifteen minutes. I compare slow jobs with historical baselines and related errors. Finally I capture run IDs, integration runtime, dependency stages and alert thresholds. I verify data retention before claiming a complete ninety-day analysis.
ADF, Data Pipelines & Modelling / Azure.technical_context: For operational analytics, route diagnostic categories from the correct ADF instance to a Log Analytics workspace. Kusto Query Language filters by time, status, resource and normalized run identifiers. Duration can be computed from start/end timestamps or reported duration fields, with explicit handling of in-progress runs, late log ingestion, time zones and duplicate activity retries. Workspace retention may be shorter than a requested ninety-day investigation; verify retention and sampling before making conclusions. Alert on sustained errors or p95 changes with enough context for run-level triage.
common_mistakes: Assuming logs exist for a period beyond configured retention
Mixing milliseconds and seconds when computing runtime
Treating ingestion time as the original activity start time

ADF, Data Pipelines & Modelling / Lakeho.question: What is medallion architecture?
ADF, Data Pipelines & Modelling / Lakeho.reference_answer: In a medallion lakehouse, Bronze holds raw incoming data and ingestion metadata so I can replay or audit a source. Silver cleans, standardizes, deduplicates and resolves update or delete semantics into reliable entities. Gold presents curated facts, dimensions or KPIs for downstream reporting. I add quality assertions at every boundary and maintain lineage. The layers are logical data contracts, not automatically separate physical systems. I also preserve access control, so a curated Gold table does not accidentally expose sensitive raw fields.
ADF, Data Pipelines & Modelling / Lakeho.technical_context: Bronze preserves source payload, ingestion metadata and replay capability; Silver validates types, deduplicates, applies CDC semantics and normalizes entities; Gold publishes stable domain metrics and dimensional aggregates. Delta Lake transaction logs enable atomic writes, schema enforcement and rollback/time travel within retention limits. Each layer has explicit quality contracts, ownership and refresh schedules. Security labels and tenant ACLs must remain in downstream tables; a Gold view is not automatically safe because it is curated. Track lineage and handle reprocessing from an immutable Bronze snapshot.
common_mistakes: Overwriting Bronze without replay history
Skipping duplicate or delete handling in Silver
Exposing restricted columns in Gold
ADF, Data Pipelines & Modelling / Lakeho.project_context: An Azure Databricks platform can use Bronze/Silver/Gold with Unity Catalog governance and ADF orchestration, testing invariants at layer transitions.

ADF, Data Pipelines & Modelling / Lakeho.question: How do ADF, ADLS, Databricks and Synapse connect?

Choose architecture based on scale, query latency and governance instead of deploying every service by default. Granting shared account keys to all services
Ignoring Gen2 hierarchical ACLs when RBAC is broad

ADF, Data Pipelines & Modelling / Lakeho.question: Compare SCD2 and SCD3.
ADF, Data Pipelines & Modelling / Lakeho.reference_answer: SCD Type 2 stores a separate row for every meaningful attribute change, typically with effective dates and a current flag. Type 3 adds columns such as previous_region and current_region, supporting only specific historical comparisons. Handle late-arriving updates, overlapping date ranges and unique current-row constraints deliberately.

Treating Type 3 as unlimited history
Ignoring late-arriving changes

ADF, Data Pipelines & Modelling / Lakeho.question: How would you model quarterly revenue?
ADF, Data Pipelines & Modelling / Lakeho.reference_answer: I begin dimensional modelling by defining the business process and the grain, such as one row per invoice line. The fact table holds measures like quantity or net sales and foreign keys to conformed date, product and customer dimensions. Dimensions supply stable descriptive context, including historical attributes when SCD Type 2 is required. To compare quarter-over-quarter revenue I must handle refunds, currency, late invoices and duplicate joins consistently. I validate totals against source accounting controls before publishing a KPI.
ADF, Data Pipelines & Modelling / Lakeho.technical_context: A star schema starts by declaring the grain of each fact record, for example one invoice line per transaction date, product and customer. Facts hold additive or semi-additive measures and surrogate keys to conformed dimensions. Calendar and slowly changing dimensions support consistent quarter comparisons and historical state. Model revenue, refunds and currency conversion explicitly rather than summing incompatible values. Enforce uniqueness at declared grain and reconcile source amounts so join fan-out does not inflate totals; many-to-many bridges require special care.
common_mistakes: Joining two detailed fact tables directly and double-counting
Ignoring refunds or exchange rates
Treating an SCD2 dimension as current-only history

ADF, Data Pipelines & Modelling / Lakeho.question: How do you reconcile source and destination data?
ADF, Data Pipelines & Modelling / Lakeho.reference_answer: A successful pipeline run only tells me its activities executed; it does not prove every record is accurate. I check expected schemas, key uniqueness, null constraints, row counts and financial or operational control totals. For incremental loads I compare the exact change window and count inserts, updates and deletes separately. When numbers differ I use anti-joins and checksums or keyed comparisons to isolate mismatches. I quarantine exceptions, document the run ID and only publish reconciled data downstream.
ADF, Data Pipelines & Modelling / Lakeho.technical_context: Build quality contracts for schema, completeness, uniqueness, referential integrity, validity and freshness. At ingestion, compare source and target counts and aggregate control totals within a consistent extraction window. For incremental upserts, compare change-set inserts/updates/deletes and check stable keys, null handling and late arrivals rather than raw full-table counts alone. Quarantine exceptions, attach run IDs and sample failing keys for deterministic replay. Alert on breaches using baselines and severity; never modify production data silently to make a metric pass.
common_mistakes: Equating row counts with complete data correctness
Comparing different extraction times
Suppressing mismatches without retaining evidence
ADF, Data Pipelines & Modelling / Lakeho.project_context: For Dev-to-QA ADF and Databricks replication, combine copy-run metrics with SQL anti-joins and controlled aggregates for missing or changed IDs.

Treating success of ingestion as data reconciliation
Claiming plant-specific achievements without evidence

Python, SQL & API Skills / SQL / Joins &.question: How do you find Hive IDs missing in SQL?
Python, SQL & API Skills / SQL / Joins &.reference_answer: An anti-join finds records on one side that do not exist on the other. If I want Hive IDs missing in a SQL temp table, Hive must be the left side. In Spark I use LEFT ANTI JOIN on the ID, and in T-SQL I often use NOT EXISTS. I check data types, null handling and duplicate IDs so the result is meaningful. This is especially useful for reconciliation after ADF or Databricks ingestion, where we must prove which source records did not arrive.
Python, SQL & API Skills / SQL / Joins &.technical_context: A left anti join returns left rows for which the right join condition finds no match. In Spark SQL use LEFT ANTI JOIN; in SQL Server use NOT EXISTS or a LEFT JOIN ... WHERE right.key IS NULL pattern with care. SQL NULL semantics make NOT IN unsafe if the subquery can return NULL, and duplicate keys may require DISTINCT depending on the business need.

Using NOT IN with nullable subquery
Confusing unmatched row count with distinct missing keys

Python, SQL & API Skills / SQL / Window.question: How would you find the most recent record per account?
Python, SQL & API Skills / SQL / Window.reference_answer: I use SQL window functions when I need information from related rows while still returning individual rows. For the latest record per account, I partition by account ID, order by update time descending with a deterministic tie-breaker and assign ROW_NUMBER. Then I select row number one. LAG and LEAD help compare adjacent values such as current and prior quarters. I check duplicate timestamps, null sort order and window frame semantics so the result is reproducible.
Python, SQL & API Skills / SQL / Window.technical_context: ROW_NUMBER, RANK, DENSE_RANK, LAG, LEAD and aggregate OVER clauses combine partition definitions, explicit ordering and frame semantics. To select the latest account record, use ROW_NUMBER over PARTITION BY account_id ORDER BY effective_at DESC, event_id DESC, then filter rn=1; the second sort key makes ties deterministic. Window functions run before final ORDER BY, and different engines differ in null ordering and default frames. For financial time series, validate period boundaries and late records before comparing lagged values.
common_mistakes: Using MAX(timestamp) join that returns duplicate ties
Omitting ORDER BY for latest-record selection
Confusing window PARTITION BY with physical storage partitions
Python, SQL & API Skills / SQL / Window.project_context: Use window ranking on Hive history tables to identify the latest snapshot before comparing with reporting SQL Server tables.

Python, SQL & API Skills / SQL / CTEs, G.question: How would you compare current and previous quarter revenue?

GROUP BY creates totals per quarter or segment, while HAVING applies a condition to the aggregated result. WHERE removes source rows first. WHERE filters input records before grouping; HAVING filters groups after aggregate calculation. Use conditional aggregation or two period CTEs to compare quarters, with a canonical date dimension, currency normalization and refund adjustments. Validate joins before grouping to avoid duplicate revenue. A CTE is a logical query expression, not necessarily materialized or a performance cache; inspect the optimizer plan.

Double-counting after a one-to-many dimension join
Assuming every CTE is physically cached

Python, SQL & API Skills / SQL / Paramet.question: Why not let an agent run arbitrary SQL?
Python, SQL & API Skills / SQL / Paramet.reference_answer: Parameterized SQL protects against injection by sending values as bind parameters rather than concatenating user text into a query. For an AI agent that is only one layer of defense. I would restrict which metrics and tables it can ask for, use a read-only role with row-level security, validate tenant context and set execution limits. If the model proposes a table or column identifier, I map it through an explicit allowlist instead of treating it as a trusted parameter.
Python, SQL & API Skills / SQL / Paramet.technical_context: Parameterized queries use database driver bind variables for values; authorization must still constrain allowed tables, columns, joins, filters, rows and query complexity. Never assume identifiers can be safely parameterized: table/column names require a separate strict allowlist or semantic query layer. Enforce read-only roles, row-level access at the database, timeouts and maximum result sizes. SQL agents should produce a structured intent mapped to approved templates, not execute arbitrary LLM-generated SQL under broad credentials.
common_mistakes: Concatenating user values into executable SQL
Thinking bind parameters authorize a tenant
Executing arbitrary model-generated DDL or write queries
Python, SQL & API Skills / SQL / Paramet.project_context: An analytics agent can select an allowlisted quarterly-revenue metric but must not generate unrestricted SELECT * FROM sensitive banking tables.

Python, SQL & API Skills / SQL / Postgre.question: How do you implement row-level security for tenants?
Python, SQL & API Skills / SQL / Postgre.reference_answer: I would create PostgreSQL tables with strong constraints and indexes, then add Supabase Auth and database row-level security. A policy should let each user see and update only records they own, with special care for inserts and ownership changes. I also protect private Storage paths and never expose a service-role key in frontend code. To verify tenant isolation I test two dedicated real user sessions for denied cross-user reads and writes; mock tests alone cannot prove that the hosted policies are correct.
Python, SQL & API Skills / SQL / Postgre.technical_context: Design relational tables with primary/foreign keys, indexes and constraints before exposing PostgREST endpoints. Supabase Auth supplies verified identity; PostgreSQL row-level security policies using auth.uid() can restrict reads and writes for user-owned or membership-scoped records. Enable and test RLS for every exposed table, check USING and WITH CHECK for ownership changes, and constrain Storage bucket paths separately. Service-role credentials bypass RLS and must never ship to the browser. Test with two actual unprivileged JWTs; frontend filters alone are not security.

Exposing the service-role key in JavaScript
Omitting WITH CHECK on ownership-sensitive writes
Python, SQL & API Skills / SQL / Postgre.project_context: Galaxy uses genai_study_* tables and private genai-study-docs; live two-account isolation verification remains separately approval-gated.

Python, SQL & API Skills / Python / List.question: When would you use a dict rather than a list?
Python, SQL & API Skills / Python / List.reference_answer: I use a list when I need an ordered, changeable sequence, a tuple for a fixed group of values, a set for distinct items and membership checks, and a dictionary for mapping keys to values. For example, a dict is better than repeatedly searching a list when I frequently need a record by ID. I still consider memory, duplicates and concurrency. A set is not a substitute for persistent idempotency storage because it disappears when the process restarts.
Python, SQL & API Skills / Python / List.technical_context: A list preserves order and allows duplicate mutable elements; a tuple fixes the sequence structure and often represents a stable record; a set offers average constant-time membership for hashable values; a dict maps hashable keys to values, preserving insertion order in modern Python. Each has different iteration, memory and equality behavior. Do not confuse tuple immutability with deep immutability of objects inside it, and do not assume set order is stable. Use explicit data classes or typed dictionaries when structured contracts grow complex.
common_mistakes: Depending on set iteration order
Assuming tuple freezes nested mutable members
Keeping production idempotency only in process memory
Python, SQL & API Skills / Python / List.project_context: A voice agent's tool router can keep route configuration in a dict and track processed idempotency keys in durable storage rather than an in-process set.

Python, SQL & API Skills / Python / Func.question: How should a Python tool report an exception?
Python, SQL & API Skills / Python / Func.reference_answer: I create small Python functions with clear inputs, outputs and one responsibility. Decorators help apply shared checks such as authentication or tracing, provided they preserve metadata and do not hide business logic. With exceptions I distinguish invalid user requests from retryable network failures and real coding errors. In an agent tool I return a structured error the orchestrator can handle. I never swallow an exception and claim a booking succeeded, and I use idempotency keys before retrying side effects.
Python, SQL & API Skills / Python / Func.technical_context: Design Python tool functions with type-checked inputs, bounded side effects and a predictable result/error schema. Decorators can add authorization, tracing, retry or validation but may obscure call order and should preserve signatures using functools.wraps. Distinguish expected domain errors (missing slot, forbidden account) from transient upstream errors eligible for bounded retries and unexpected defects requiring alerts. Do not catch Exception and return fabricated success. For financial or booking writes, retry only under an idempotency contract and avoid logging sensitive request payloads.

Applying retries to non-idempotent writes
Using decorators that lose function names or authorization context
Python, SQL & API Skills / Python / Func.project_context: A banking appointment tool can report validation, forbidden, provider timeout and success as distinct outcomes to a LangGraph supervisor.

Python, SQL & API Skills / Python / File.question: How would you process a fixed-width file?
Python, SQL & API Skills / Python / File.reference_answer: For fixed-width files I start with the interface document: encoding, record length, field offsets, padding and header or trailer rules. I slice fields by declared positions, parse types explicitly and quarantine malformed records with line numbers. I use JSON schema validation for metadata and regex for limited patterns, not as a substitute for checking the complete file contract. Before publishing the transformed file I reconcile record counts and control totals against the input.

First determine encoding because multibyte UTF-8 changes byte offsets, normalize line endings, identify header/detail/trailer types and validate each slice without silently trimming significant zeros. JSON parsing needs schema validation and maximum size/depth guards; regular expressions can capture bounded field patterns but are not a universal replacement for a structured parser. Reject unexpected record lengths, preserve bad-line evidence and reconcile trailer control totals.

Accepting regex matches without full-record validation
Dropping leading zeros from identifiers

Python, SQL & API Skills / Python / REST.question: How do you build a callable tool API?

I make reads safe and require confirmation plus an idempotency key for bookings or other writes. I add timeouts, quotas, tracing and tests for expired tokens, forbidden accounts and partial provider failures. The OpenAPI schema describes capability; it does not enforce authorization automatically.

Using blocking SDK calls without concurrency planning
Allowing arbitrary backend URLs in model tool arguments

Python, SQL & API Skills / Python / Asyn.question: How can you call independent services concurrently?
Python, SQL & API Skills / Python / Asyn.reference_answer: I use Python asyncio when a workload waits on independent network or database operations. I can launch multiple calls with gather or TaskGroup, but I set timeouts, limit concurrency and handle partial failures. If I send hundreds of calls without a semaphore, I may overload a provider or hit throttling. CPU-heavy Python code still blocks the event loop unless moved elsewhere. For banking tools I also avoid racing state-changing operations and use idempotency and explicit workflow order.
Python, SQL & API Skills / Python / Asyn.technical_context: In asyncio, coroutines yield while waiting for nonblocking operations. Use asyncio.gather or TaskGroup for independent requests while protecting shared cancellation and propagating errors intentionally. Bound concurrency with a semaphore and provider rate limits; implement per-call deadlines, retry budgets and circuit breaking. CPU-bound parsing or model preprocessing needs worker processes, native extensions or separate tasks rather than blocking the event loop. For side effects, concurrent writes require ordering and idempotency, not just gather.
common_mistakes: Launching unbounded tasks against a throttled API
Assuming asyncio speeds up CPU-heavy pure Python
Retrying non-idempotent writes concurrently
Python, SQL & API Skills / Python / Asyn.project_context: A voice agent may overlap retrieval and profile reads but must not execute booking and payment writes concurrently without explicit ordering.

Python, SQL & API Skills / Python / PySp.question: How do you handle malformed records in Spark?

I inspect explain plans, watch for shuffle skew and enforce correct keys before writing Delta tables. Finally I reconcile accepted and rejected record totals.

Inspect physical plans for shuffles, skew, broadcast eligibility and partition pruning. Using row-by-row Python UDFs unnecessarily

LLMOps, Monitoring & CI/CD / Automation.question: What must pass before an AI deployment merges?

LLMOps, Monitoring & CI/CD / Automation.question: How do you handle service keys in multiple environments?

Reusing production secrets in development
Logging resolved secret strings during troubleshooting
LLMOps, Monitoring & CI/CD / Automation.project_context: For Galaxy, public runtime configuration must never include Azure Speech or model provider keys; no secure broker is deployed yet.

LLMOps, Monitoring & CI/CD / Runtime mon.question: How do you trace a bad voice interaction?
LLMOps, Monitoring & CI/CD / Runtime mon.reference_answer: I add a correlation ID for the overall call and a trace ID for each conversational turn, then propagate those identifiers across STT, retrieval, model, tool and TTS spans. When a user reports a wrong or slow reply, I can see the exact step, its outcome and its dependency timings. Traces should contain metadata and redacted identifiers, not secret tokens or full private conversations. I combine those spans with logs and metrics to distinguish timeouts, poor retrieval and model errors.
LLMOps, Monitoring & CI/CD / Runtime mon.technical_context: Propagate a stable trace context such as W3C traceparent across WebSocket connection, audio ingress, STT, agent orchestration, retrieval, tools, LLM and TTS. Create child spans with service name, model deployment, route, timestamp, outcome and safe durations, but redact user speech, account balances, secrets and raw tokens. Distinguish one phone call ID from multiple utterance/turn IDs and one logical retry from each attempt. Sample based on risk and latency while keeping enough operational evidence for failures; never fabricate traces retroactively.
common_mistakes: Using different request IDs with no parent correlation
Logging bank balance or audio as debug payload
Treating an error status in one child span as complete root cause
LLMOps, Monitoring & CI/CD / Runtime mon.project_context: Use call-scoped identifiers in banking voice assistant design so a root-cause investigation can follow Functions and WebSocket boundaries.

LLMOps, Monitoring & CI/CD / Runtime mon.question: How do you monitor token usage?
LLMOps, Monitoring & CI/CD / Runtime mon.reference_answer: For token monitoring I record input tokens, output tokens, cached tokens and model version for each completed call, along with retries and failures. I calculate an estimated cost using the provider's current contractual rate and reconcile the result with bills. I also track cost per successful task because a cheap response that triggers several retries may be more expensive overall. I set token budgets, cap context and evaluate caching without logging private prompts or exposing tenant-specific spending.
LLMOps, Monitoring & CI/CD / Runtime mon.technical_context: Capture provider-reported input, output and cached-token usage per model, deployment and logical request, distinguishing request retries and partial streams. Apply a versioned price table with currency and contract date for estimated spend and reconcile periodically against actual billing. Add budgets for maximum context size, retrieval chunks, response length, tool rounds and evaluation sample rate. Attribute costs by tenant with pseudonymous IDs and avoid exporting prompts with private content. Track cost per successful task, not only token totals.
common_mistakes: Multiplying all tokens by one universal rate
Counting a retry as a new successful task
Logging prompt bodies when only token totals are needed
LLMOps, Monitoring & CI/CD / Runtime mon.project_context: The Galaxy evaluator currently is not deployed; CI and design docs should not report model-token spend as live production telemetry.

LLMOps, Monitoring & CI/CD / Runtime mon.question: Why can the first chat response be slow?
LLMOps, Monitoring & CI/CD / Runtime mon.reference_answer: When a user says the first answer is slow, I measure the full critical path: client connection, speech recognition, retrieval, model queue and generation, tool calls, speech synthesis and playback. I separate first-audio delay from total answer time and compare warm versus cold starts. I also use p95 rather than averages alone. If a function cold start or serial external tool dominates, changing the LLM temperature will not fix it. I tune the measured bottleneck.
LLMOps, Monitoring & CI/CD / Runtime mon.technical_context: Instrument client network, cold start, authentication, STT endpointing, retrieval, reranking, model queue/prefill/decode, sequential tool calls, TTS synthesis and audio playback. Measure first-token/first-audio latency separately from final completion, as perceived responsiveness matters for conversation. Critical-path analysis accounts for concurrent stages: summing parallel spans overstates wall time. Segment p50/p95 by deployment, language, call type and warm/cold start; apply time budgets and fallback policies to dominant delays before tuning unrelated components.
common_mistakes: Adding overlapping parallel spans as if sequential
Reporting only server model time
Ignoring phone audio endpointing or network jitter
LLMOps, Monitoring & CI/CD / Runtime mon.project_context: For the voice assistant architecture, endpointing silence thresholds, WebSocket connection setup and speech playback can dominate first response.

LLMOps, Monitoring & CI/CD / Runtime mon.question: How do you diagnose a booking tool failure?
LLMOps, Monitoring & CI/CD / Runtime mon.reference_answer: I first inspect the tool status, latency, input validation and authenticated context. A 403 needs an authorization fix, not a retry, whereas a 429 or temporary 503 may be recoverable after backoff. If a booking request times out, I cannot assume it failed or succeeded. I check the operation using an idempotency key or transaction ID before repeating it. The agent should communicate uncertainty clearly and offer safe follow-up or human assistance rather than invent a success.
LLMOps, Monitoring & CI/CD / Runtime mon.technical_context: Tool failure modes include input validation, access denial, upstream 429/5xx, timeout, schema drift and uncertain commit after request disconnect. Separate read-only retries from state-changing calls: writes require idempotency keys or reconciliation lookup before retrying. Set bounded exponential backoff with jitter for transient failures and a circuit breaker when a provider is unhealthy. The agent state must retain pending intent, show a clear failure or uncertainty message and support human handoff without exposing internal traces or guessing a booking confirmation.
common_mistakes: Retrying booking writes without idempotency
Hiding a 403 by asking the model to try different credentials
Reporting success merely because a request was sent
LLMOps, Monitoring & CI/CD / Runtime mon.project_context: For a clinic or banking appointment assistant, verify the appointment ID before reading a voice confirmation to the caller.

LLMOps, Monitoring & CI/CD / Runtime mon.question: What production dashboard would you build?
LLMOps, Monitoring & CI/CD / Runtime mon.reference_answer: I create a production dashboard around user task completion, failure rate, p95 response latency, model/tool errors, grounding quality and cost. The most important view tells us whether customers can complete the journey, not just whether a service returns HTTP 200. I configure sustained error-budget or threshold alerts with clear ownership and a trace link. I avoid high-cardinality personal identifiers and document which quality scores come from automated judges versus human reviews.
LLMOps, Monitoring & CI/CD / Runtime mon.technical_context: Track availability, task success, user-visible error rate, p50/p95 latency, tool and provider 429/5xx, STT failure, retrieval miss, groundedness sampled on approved traces, and cost per completed task. Define SLO windows and alert on burn-rate or sustained anomalies rather than one noisy point. Ensure metrics carry safe dimensions such as version, region and route, but not account balances or direct user identifiers. Separate automated quality indicators from human-labeled correctness; dashboards should provide links to redacted traces, not fabricated explanations.
common_mistakes: Alerting on every single transient model failure
Using request success as proxy for appointment success
Leaking personal details in dashboard labels
LLMOps, Monitoring & CI/CD / Runtime mon.project_context: For Galaxy, a monitoring plan can cover the future evaluator and Speech broker; no deployed backend reliability dashboard exists yet.

LLMOps, Monitoring & CI/CD / Runtime mon.question: A user says the answer is wrong: what are your steps?
LLMOps, Monitoring & CI/CD / Runtime mon.reference_answer: I would ask for a reproducible example and the relevant trace rather than immediately changing the prompt. First I confirm user identity and whether the correct source existed and was accessible at that time. Then I inspect STT, retrieval, reranker, model context and tool outputs to locate the first incorrect stage. I fix that stage and add a golden regression test, including any tenant-isolation case. Finally I compare quality and latency before and after release.
LLMOps, Monitoring & CI/CD / Runtime mon.technical_context: Collect a consented session/trace reference and classify wrong output by authorization, stale index, retrieval recall, reranking, context assembly, prompt interpretation, model behavior or tool side effect. Inspect the evidence shown to the model and the true source at the incident time. Apply a narrow repair: fix ACLs or ingestion for missing documents, retrieval tuning for missed evidence, tool/schema handling for incorrect actions, or prompt/model evaluation for groundedness errors. Add a regression fixture, compare against labeled baseline and monitor deployment cohorts.
common_mistakes: Calling every incorrect answer a hallucination
Fixing the prompt when the index was stale
Using private production data directly as a public golden fixture
LLMOps, Monitoring & CI/CD / Runtime mon.project_context: For a banking voice answer complaint, correlate speech transcript and account-tool response before concluding the LLM hallucinated.

LLMOps, Monitoring & CI/CD / Production.question: How do you debug a slow banking call end to end?
LLMOps, Monitoring & CI/CD / Production.reference_answer: For a slow banking call I would use a stable call ID and a separate turn ID for each utterance. I propagate trace context through the telephony WebSocket, speech recognition, agent nodes, retrieval, model inference, authorized tools and TTS. This lets me identify whether the delay came from endpointing, model queue time or an external banking API. I also mark retries and cancellations and redact customer details. Without that correlation, individual service logs can tell conflicting stories.
LLMOps, Monitoring & CI/CD / Production.technical_context: Use a call ID per phone session and a turn ID per utterance, propagated from WebSocket connection through STT, LangGraph state, model, retrieval and tool invocation to TTS playback. Link asynchronous spans using traceparent or explicit span links, including reconnects and retries. Observe input audio timestamps, silence endpointing, provider token delays and downstream API duration without storing customer speech or account data in traces. For overlapping turns, label cancellation generations so stale TTS or booking callbacks cannot be attached to the new turn.
common_mistakes: Using one global trace ID for every call
Storing raw speech and balances in traces
Confusing canceled callbacks with valid current-turn output
LLMOps, Monitoring & CI/CD / Production.project_context: The Galaxy frontend mic regression suite validates stale callbacks offline; distributed traces for a deployed banking system remain a design goal.

Anomaly Detection & Agentic RCA / Statis.question: What baseline do you use for pipeline runtime?
Anomaly Detection & Agentic RCA / Statis.reference_answer: I build a runtime baseline from comparable historical runs of the same pipeline, separating daily and month-end workloads or different job cluster sizes. Median and median absolute deviation are useful when a few incidents would distort an average. I also normalize for input volume and exclude failed or incomplete runs from healthy statistics. When a new run exceeds its appropriate distribution I flag it and show the actual history. The baseline should be reviewable, not a black-box claim that every long run is broken.
Anomaly Detection & Agentic RCA / Statis.technical_context: Segment duration history by pipeline, schedule window, workload size, cluster class and weekday seasonality. Exclude canceled runs, outages and known incident periods from a healthy baseline while keeping those events for audit. Use median and median absolute deviation for robust central tendency and spread, with a minimum sample count and fallback for near-zero MAD. Compare normalized runtime per input volume when data sizes vary, and periodically recompute thresholds without allowing persistent degradation to redefine healthy performance silently.
common_mistakes: Comparing month-end jobs with daily micro-batches
Including known outages as healthy baseline
Dividing by MAD without handling zero dispersion
Anomaly Detection & Agentic RCA / Statis.project_context: A Databricks/ADF anomaly detector can use scheduled-run history to flag slow workloads before an RCA assistant summarizes trace evidence.

Anomaly Detection & Agentic RCA / Statis.question: Why use MAD instead of standard deviation?
Anomaly Detection & Agentic RCA / Statis.reference_answer: We used median and median absolute deviation for pipeline duration anomalies because production runtimes can contain large spikes that distort mean and standard deviation. We calculated robust baselines per comparable pipeline window, classified anomalies and passed correlated logs to an RCA assistant for actionable explanations. I distinguish abnormal duration from a proven cause, use minimum sample requirements and guard a zero MAD denominator. Critical alerts also consider SLA breach and downstream impact, not only statistical distance.
Anomaly Detection & Agentic RCA / Statis.technical_context: Median absolute deviation is median(|x_i−median(x)|), robust against extreme outliers. A robust z-like score can use 0.6745(x−median)/MAD when MAD>0. Add minimum sample thresholds, segmentation by pipeline/load window and special handling for zero MAD.
common_mistakes: Claiming MAD is mean absolute deviation
Using one baseline across dissimilar pipelines
Dividing by zero when MAD=0
Anomaly Detection & Agentic RCA / Statis.project_context: Your RCA project establishes per-pipeline duration baselines, labels warnings/critical runs and enriches anomalies using Supabase activity logs and dependency metadata.

Anomaly Detection & Agentic RCA / Statis.question: How do you decide if a run is critical?
Anomaly Detection & Agentic RCA / Statis.reference_answer: I do not map all anomalies to severity only from a Z-score. I combine duration deviation with a pipeline's SLA, number of affected retries, downstream dependencies and business consequences. A warning could be an unusual but recoverable delay, while critical means a missed deadline or impact to an important feed. I add hysteresis so noisy metrics do not flip status on every sample. Every alert should show its threshold, run ID and evidence so a support team can defend the decision.
Anomaly Detection & Agentic RCA / Statis.technical_context: Combine a robust anomaly score with hard SLA thresholds, repeated failures, dependency criticality and downstream business impact. A normal band fits expected distribution and SLO; warning may indicate elevated duration or one missing feed; critical requires breached deadline, significant evidence of blockage or safety-sensitive effect. Use hysteresis and cool-down to reduce alert flapping and maintain overrides for known maintenance periods. Keep thresholds versioned, justify why a pipeline is business-critical and display the input evidence to the operator.
common_mistakes: Hardcoding identical thresholds for every pipeline
Paging for transient noise without persistence checks
Automatically downgrading a confirmed SLA breach because average is low
Anomaly Detection & Agentic RCA / Statis.project_context: For an agentic RCA monitor, severity dictates whether the agent only comments, opens a ticket or pages the responsible SME.

Anomaly Detection & Agentic RCA / Statis.question: What schema would you create for anomalies?
Anomaly Detection & Agentic RCA / Statis.reference_answer: I would design separate tables for pipeline definitions, completed runs, anomalies and the investigation or ticket lifecycle. A run stores start, end, status and workload details. An anomaly record stores the detector version, baseline and evidence that justified its severity. This makes it possible to reproduce decisions later. I use stable run IDs for idempotency, indexes for time-based analysis and row-level security where tenants share a database. I avoid mixing arbitrary LLM explanations into authoritative raw measurements.
Anomaly Detection & Agentic RCA / Statis.technical_context: A minimal schema includes pipeline identity, run ID, schedule window, started/ended timestamps, input volume, compute type and observed duration. Anomaly events reference the run plus baseline version, score, severity, threshold, detector version and evidence URI. RCA annotations and ticket links are separate append-only records with status transitions. Index (pipeline_id, run_start) and unique run IDs; enforce row-level tenant/owner scope if Supabase is shared, and redact raw credentials and business-sensitive fields. Prefer idempotent inserts/upserts on run ID.
common_mistakes: Overwriting historical anomaly decisions without versioning
Giving the RCA agent write access to all tables
Storing secret-bearing activity payloads in general telemetry
Anomaly Detection & Agentic RCA / Statis.project_context: A conceptual anomaly service can persist only its own dedicated run metadata; this does not grant permission to write Galaxy or other shared Supabase tables.

Anomaly Detection & Agentic RCA / Root-c.question: Which activity made a pipeline slow?
Anomaly Detection & Agentic RCA / Root-c.reference_answer: I use the pipeline run ID to retrieve activity attempts and the configured dependency graph. Then I compare start and end times, retries and stage-level baselines to find which activity actually delayed the dependent path. When activities run in parallel, I do not simply add their durations. I also inspect whether the slow stage suffered integration-runtime saturation, source throttling or Spark skew. The output should distinguish observed bottlenecks from an unverified root-cause hypothesis.
Anomaly Detection & Agentic RCA / Root-c.technical_context: Join parent pipeline runs to activity attempts by run ID, activity name, retry number, start/end timestamps and dependency edges. Construct a DAG from the pipeline definition and compute the longest blocking path, accounting for parallel activities and retries. Compare stage runtimes to per-stage baselines; do not sum unrelated parallel waits or blame the final activity because it finished last. Correlate ADF activity errors, integration runtime load, external service throttling and Databricks job duration before identifying a likely causal contributor.
common_mistakes: Summing durations of parallel stages
Selecting last completed activity as root cause without graph analysis
Ignoring retries that restart an activity
Anomaly Detection & Agentic RCA / Root-c.project_context: An anomaly RCA assistant can present a ranked bottleneck candidate with links to ADF activity logs and Spark stage metrics.

Anomaly Detection & Agentic RCA / Root-c.question: What is the value of a materialized RCA view?
Anomaly Detection & Agentic RCA / Root-c.reference_answer: A materialized RCA view stores a precomputed join of pipeline history, activity logs and anomaly metadata so the assistant does not rebuild a costly query for every investigation. I define the expected refresh interval and make the last refresh visible. I also check permissions, uniqueness and source lineage. The agent must not present stale output as a live result. I would benchmark full versus incremental maintenance according to the capabilities of the actual platform and version.
Anomaly Detection & Agentic RCA / Root-c.technical_context: A materialized view persists results of a defined query for efficient repeated consumption; it needs a refresh policy, freshness indication and source lineage. Join pipeline runs, activity attempts, anomaly scores and known dependency edges into stable columns that an authorized analysis tool can query. Distinguish incremental refresh availability across engines and product versions; do not assume every Databricks declarative pipeline or SQL engine supports the same maintenance semantics. Use schema evolution gates, tenant filters and stale-view detection so an agent does not confuse yesterday's precomputed result with live status.
common_mistakes: Calling any temporary view materialized
Assuming precomputed data is always current
Allowing a model to bypass row filters through a shared view
Anomaly Detection & Agentic RCA / Root-c.project_context: A Databricks SQL materialized view can support an anomaly RCA agent only when freshness, authorization and refresh failures are monitored.

Anomaly Detection & Agentic RCA / Root-c.question: How does an RCA assistant avoid inventing causes?
Anomaly Detection & Agentic RCA / Root-c.reference_answer: I separate facts from interpretation. SQL tools return actual pipeline durations, error codes and dependency stages, while RAG retrieves operational runbooks and prior approved incidents. The model can combine those sources into a ranked RCA hypothesis with citations, but it must not state that a cause is confirmed without matching evidence. I validate tenant access, show run IDs and timestamps, and allow the SME to correct or reject the suggestion. Any remediation remains separately authorized.
Anomaly Detection & Agentic RCA / Root-c.technical_context: An RCA assistant should first retrieve authoritative run metrics, activity logs and dependency path from allowlisted SQL queries. Retrieve runbooks, ticket histories and platform documentation via ACL-filtered hybrid search; rerank and cite passages alongside exact run IDs and timestamps. The model synthesizes hypotheses with confidence and contradictory evidence rather than asserting causality. Guard against prompt injection in log messages and documents, verify tool permissions, and require human validation before operational changes or ticket escalation.
common_mistakes: Passing free-form model SQL with privileged credentials
Calling correlation definitive causation
Trusting instructions embedded in activity log text
Anomaly Detection & Agentic RCA / Root-c.project_context: The anomaly detection and agentic RCA concept combines deterministic monitoring with retrieval-backed explanation and an SME handoff.

Anomaly Detection & Agentic RCA / Root-c.question: How do you shorten time to root cause?
Anomaly Detection & Agentic RCA / Root-c.reference_answer: When a pipeline is genuinely critical, I create a support ticket containing the affected run, priority, measured delay, failed activity, evidence links and a suggested investigation path. I use an incident key to avoid duplicate tickets on repeated monitoring polls. The agent's explanation is labeled as a hypothesis until an SME validates it. I track response and resolution against SLA and update the ticket when new evidence appears. High-impact remediation should require human approval.
Anomaly Detection & Agentic RCA / Root-c.technical_context: Open a ticket only after severity rules and routing rules authorize it. Create or reuse a stable incident key from affected pipeline, window and failure signature so repeated checks do not flood support queues. Attach the run ID, SLA/deadline, activity timings, redacted log links, suspected causes labeled as hypotheses and mitigation context. Provide confirmation for impact-changing actions. Track acknowledgement, handoff, resolution time and reopen rate; learn from SME feedback without silently altering detector thresholds.
common_mistakes: Creating a ticket for every anomaly polling event
Marking a model hypothesis as confirmed root cause
Sharing unredacted credentials in incident details
Anomaly Detection & Agentic RCA / Root-c.project_context: A support agent can route anomaly RCA summaries to an SME, but human-validated root cause remains distinct from generated suggestion.

Anomaly Detection & Agentic RCA / Root-c.question: How would you quantify business impact?
Anomaly Detection & Agentic RCA / Root-c.reference_answer: I use governance to know which data sources are authoritative, who can access them and how a reported RCA can be audited. For business impact, I compare detection, investigation and resolution times against a fair pre-implementation baseline. I also measure SLA misses and false-alert burden so a faster dashboard is not automatically treated as a business win. Any claimed percentage improvement needs comparable incidents and documented ticket outcomes. The model's role is to assist investigation, not replace ownership.
Anomaly Detection & Agentic RCA / Root-c.technical_context: Use catalogs and lineage to identify source datasets, owners, transformations and authoritative KPIs. Apply least-privilege data access, retention, audit events and change review for RCA annotations. Quantify operational impact with pre/post baselines: mean/median time to detect, time to acknowledge, time to identify cause, SLA breach frequency and resolved incidents per on-call hour. Normalize comparisons for incident severity and volume, distinguish correlation from attribution, and avoid claiming cost savings absent controlled evidence.
common_mistakes: Equating ticket creation with root-cause resolution
Claiming financial savings without cost evidence
Ignoring false alarms and on-call workload
Anomaly Detection & Agentic RCA / Root-c.project_context: Unity Catalog governance and an agentic RCA workflow may contribute to faster support resolution; real impact values require ticket system evidence.

Enterprise File Processing AI / File par.question: How can one ingestion engine support many formats?
Enterprise File Processing AI / File par.reference_answer: I would build a metadata-driven ingestion engine that selects an approved format definition for each input. A fixed-width format needs encoding, record lengths, offsets and data types, while a delimited format needs delimiter, quoting and escape rules. Both emit a normalized record with source location and error metadata. I validate header and trailer controls, reject malformed records into quarantine and compare totals before publishing. The engine is generic, but the rules are explicit and versioned.
Enterprise File Processing AI / File par.technical_context: A format contract describes character encoding, line endings, row kinds, required length, field name, start offset and width, delimiter/quote/escape rules, and header/trailer expectations. Fixed-width offsets may refer to bytes, not Unicode characters; delimited formats need quoted delimiter and embedded newline handling. Select a versioned contract by trusted source and validate schema before processing. Parse incrementally, quarantine malformed records, and reconcile physical row count with declared trailer count. Retain source fingerprints for deterministic replay.
